item.title: Desert Hot Springs Hosting Active Transportation Workshop
item.description: The City of Desert Hot Springs is inviting residents to help shape the future of local transportation.An Active Transportation Plan Update Workshop will be held February 26th from 5 to 7 p.m. at City Hall. The drop-in, open house-style event will give community members a chance to review proposed bicycle and pedestrian networks, ask questions, and share ideas aimed at improving safety and connectivity throughout the city.The workshop will take place in the council chambers on Palm Drive. item.title: Supreme Court adopts automated software to help justices avoid conflicts of interest
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court announced it will begin using automated software to help justices determine when they should step aside from cases involving potential conflicts of interest.According to the court, the system will compare the names of parties and attorneys involved in a case with lists maintained by each justice identifying individuals, organizations, or financial interests that could present a conflict. item.title: St. Theresa Students Celebrate Modernism Week with Palm Springs-Inspired Showcase
item.description: To celebrate Palm Springs Modernism Week, St. Theresa Catholic School in Palm Springs held its own special event, highlighting student creativity and the city’s iconic architectural roots.As part of a long-running sixth-grade project, students designed and built detailed housing models that embody the essence of Palm Springs modernism. item.title: Fresh Snow, Winter Games Events Draw Crowds to Big Bear
item.description: With fresh snow on the ground and clear blue skies overhead, conditions are ideal at Big Bear Mountain Resort.Resort officials say visitors can expect sunshine and strong snow coverage across the mountain, thanks in large part to extensive snowmaking efforts during one of the driest winters in the West. item.title: Missing Indio Woman Found Safe After Silver Alert Deactivated
item.description: A woman reported missing last year in Indio has been safely located, according to the California Highway Patrol. Officials confirmed the Silver Alert issued for 78-year-old Laura Ann Brown has now been deactivated.Brown was last seen in November near the intersection of Jefferson Street and Avenue 48, prompting concerns for her safety and the issuance of the alert to help locate her. item.title: Palm Springs Completes Wind Wall to Reduce Blowing Sand and Improve Driver Safety
item.description: Drivers traveling along North Gene Autry Trail in Palm Springs will soon notice improved conditions thanks to the completion of a new wind wall aimed at reducing blowing sand and hazardous visibility issues. item.description: The Palm Springs International Jazz Festival returns this week, bringing an exciting lineup of renowned performers and live music to the Coachella Valley.The musical celebration begins Thursday and runs through February 22, featuring performances from some of the biggest names in jazz. item.title: The Prestige continues play at the Norman Course at PGA West
item.description: Division one men's golf is on full display this week in La Quinta as the tournament enters the final day on Wednesday from the Norman Course at PGA West. Our Caitlyn Kelley has more. For more Coachella Valley News visit NBCPalmSprings.com

item.title: Palm Desert Woman Redefines Strength at 96
item.description: At 96 years young, a Palm Desert woman is redefining what transformation really means.Jean walked into Desert Fitness Collective determined to preserve the strength she needs to live independently after struggling to lift a 20 pound bag of fertilizer in her yard.Months later, she was deadlifting more than 150 pounds. A photo of the lift went viral, with some questioning whether it was real.Her trainer Cheryl says Jean’s progress is proof it is never too late to start strength training. For more
